method: Manual reading of every complete prompt and answer under the frozen rubric. A genuine detected issue is separate from an entirely grounded, causally cited and production-accepted review. Correct paraphrases and causal alternative citations are allowed; every additional material claim must be supported. Empty and malformed answers are retained. Hash-bound individual fragments preserve the readings; this helper only combines them and assigns no labels.

rubric.method: Read each complete response against its exact prompt, visible code and repository rules. Preserve response/model/prompt hashes and case-specific reasoning.
rubric.production_usable: Unchanged production parseReview accepts the complete response and available changed-line citations.
rubric.genuine_issue_detected: At least one supported concrete mechanism with an available causally appropriate citation, even if unsupported extras spoil the complete review.
rubric.full_review_pass: Concern: production accepted, real cited issue, every material claim/finding supported, no unsupported extra findings. Clean: production accepted empty findings.
rubric.pairs: Both concern and clean must pass fully; separately report mere presence and token decisions.
rubric.alternatives: Gold wording and canonical citation are not mandatory; any changed line with a valid causal connection is allowed, including either side of harmful no-op replacements.
rubric.precision: Awkward but meaningful explanations can pass. Separate detected real issues from inaccurate elaborations; retain explicitly reasoned sensitivity judgments if a claim is ambiguous.

cases.raw_response: {"findings":[{"line_id":1,"reason":"Removing the only required fclose in peek.c allows access to the stream before returning. Equivalent to removing the only required fclose in peek.c allows access to the stream before returning."}]}

parsed_findings.reason: Removing the only required fclose in peek.c allows access to the stream before returning. Equivalent to removing the only required fclose in peek.c allows access to the stream before returning.

supported_fragments: The change removes the only fclose in peek.c, which the supplied rule requires before returning.
After this deletion the successfully opened stream remains open and available at the point before return.
judgment.note: The response explicitly recognizes removal of the only required fclose and cites its exact removed line. This identifies the concrete violation of the supplied close-before-return contract. The awkward allows access wording is read as the stream remaining open at the point before return; it does not assert an additional executed read. The repeated sentence adds no different factual claim. Sensitivity: interpreting allows access as newly enabling the earlier fgetc would make that elaboration unsupported, because fgetc already precedes the changed line in both versions. The response does not name that earlier call; the primary reading is continued availability after the former close point. Under the stricter reading genuine issue detection remains true, while all-material-claims and full-review pass would become false. The clean counterpart still fails, so the pair score remains zero.
